title: Customer risk profile & evidence heatmap (questionnaire synthesis) - WIP
content:
Purpose:
This working doc condenses answers for common customer security questionnaires into a risk-oriented summary and an evidence heatmap tailored to enterprise buyers. Focus is on bridging RBAC v2 design decisions, audit-log schema, and SIEM export evidence so sales/CS can assemble a short packet (1–2 pages) + attachments for low-friction assessment responses.

Why this doc exists (context):
- We get a lot of repeat questionnaire asks around access controls, auditability, and log export.
- Customers generally want: an executive paragraph, a short technical assurance section, and direct artifacts they can validate in an intake call or via S3 share.
- This doc proposes a template heatmap that maps questionnaire claims -> strength of evidence we can provide automatically vs manual artifact.

Scope / audience:
- Primary: Solutions Engineering / Customer Security teams preparing responses for RFPs and security questionnaires (Vendors, SaaS due diligence).
- Secondary: Product + SRE for clarifications about what artifacts we can reliably export.

High-level guidance for responders:
- Lead with an "assurance summary": 3 lines that cite our controls and a pointer to attached artifacts (audit-log sample, RBAC role export, SIEM ingestion config).
- For technical reviewers include: sample audit log snippet (sanitized), SIEM mapping guidance, and the RBAC v2 roles/permissions export (CSV).
- Call out any customer-specific deployment differences (hosted vs dedicated vs private) because evidence availability differs.

Customer Risk Profile Heatmap (single-page canonical):
- Columns: Questionnaire area, Typical customer concern, Evidence we can provide, Evidence type, Confidence (High/Med/Low), Owner for artifact
- Example rows (abbreviated):
  * Authentication & identity: Concern = 3rd-party SSO lifecycle, Evidence = SAML metadata + auth logs, Type = automated export, Confidence = High, Owner = infra-iam
  * Admin role separation: Concern = can we see who is org-admin, Evidence = RBAC v2 role-export CSV + change history, Type = manual export (on request) / semi-automated, Confidence = Med, Owner = product-security
  * Auditability of prompts/requests: Concern = request-level audit trail, Evidence = sample audit-log (tokenized), Type = automated, Confidence = High, Owner = platform-logging
  * SIEM ingestion proof: Concern = can we ship logs to customer's SIEM, Evidence = example config + test payload, Type = automated + docs, Confidence = High, Owner = observability
  * Data residency / export: Concern = can logs be isolated to region X, Evidence = deployment manifest + export controls, Type = manual, Confidence = Med, Owner = private-deployments

Heatmap interpretation rules:
- High: Evidence exists and can be exported via self-serve or scripted runbook without engineering change.
- Medium: Evidence exists but requires access review and a support ticket or gated tooling.
- Low: Evidence requires engineering work or is not retained by default (may require custom retention or new instrumentation).

Sample short assurance narrative (customer-facing):
"Redwood Inference enforces role-based separation of duties through RBAC v2; role definitions and assignment history are captured in our audit logs. Authentication is delegated to customer-managed IdPs (SAML/OIDC) where required. We can provide a sanitized audit-log sample and a role-export CSV for customer review; for SIEM ingestion we provide example mapping and a test dry-run payload. For Dedicated or Private deployments, we can also configure region-locked log exports on request."

Evidence artifacts we recommend attaching to initial responses:
- Sanitized audit-log sample (7–14 days of representative entries, redacted PII).
- RBAC v2 role-export CSV and a brief legend that maps role -> permissions.
- SIEM mapping example (Splunk HEC/CEF/ELK JSON) and sample ingestion config.
- Link to architecture diagram for the deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Short retention/TTL table for logs and backups.

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields) — provide as part of attachment and in-document sample. Note: include only pseudo-sample values; real exports are sanitized.
- fields: timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, user_id, user_email (redacted), principal_type (service|user), action, resource_type, resource_id, role_changes (if any), outcome (success|failure), ip_address (redacted/hashed), geo, request_latency_ms, model, token_count, kv_cache_hit, trace_id

SanitizedAuditLog sample (one line, pseudo-JSON, for inclusion in the packet):
{"timestamp":"2024-11-18T15:24:02Z","tenant_id":"T-xxxxxxxx","request_id":"r-abc123","user_id":"u-xxxxx","principal_type":"user","action":"completion.create","resource_type":"model-version","resource_id":"m-redwood-13b-v2","outcome":"success","request_latency_ms":"82","model":"redwood-13b-v2","token_count":"48","trace_id":"trace-zz-001"}

SIEM ingestion & mapping guidance (concise):
- We support: HTTP ingestion (Splunk HEC), S3 delivery (for customer SIEM pickup), and syslog-forward via Fluentd/Fluent Bit in Private installs.
- Recommended mapping: timestamp -> @timestamp, tenant_id -> host/tenant, action -> event.action, outcome -> event.outcome, request_id -> event.id, model -> labels.model.
- Example Splunk HEC sample payload: Content-Type: application/json
{
  "events": [ {"time": 1700000000, "host": "tenant-xyz", "event": {"action":"completion.create","outcome":"success","request_id":"r-abc123","model":"redwood-13b-v2"}} ]
}

RBAC v2 implications for questionnaire answers (quick primer):
- RBAC v2 introduces: scoped roles (org/project/model), time-bound grants (expiring tokens/roles), and delegated role admins.
- Typical customer Qs: "Can you show a list of role owners and recent role changes?" -> Answer: we can export role list + assignment change events from audit logs; for hosted mode we provide a sanitized CSV; for Private we can run full export into customer-provided S3.
- Example Q-to-evidence mapping:
  Q: "How do you prevent privilege creep?" -> Evidence: role review cadence doc (PDF), role assignment audit entries (audit-log sample), automation rule (Lambda) that flags stale role assignments older than 90 days.

Automation & evidence packaging playbook (recommended runbook):
1) Intake: CS opens "Evidence Package" ticket with customer id, deployment type, required artifacts, desired redaction level.
2) Scripted exports: platform-logging job produces sanitized audit-log slice (date range, tenant filter). Output -> S3 temp bucket with restricted ACL.
3) RBAC export: product-script exports CSV of roles and memberships, strips PII.
4) SIEM test payload: observability generates a signed test payload and sample HEC/S3 config.
5) Package: zip + index.txt + README, uploaded to customer's share (S3 presigned URL or secure transfer).
6) Notification: CS notifies customer and schedules review call (15–30m).

Automation constraints / caveats:
- For hosted tenants we apply redaction (email -> u-****@example.com) and limit sampling to representative requests to avoid exposing user data.
- For Dedicated/Private with customer-owned infra, we can provide raw exports assuming contractually agreed data handling and SC.
- Some artifacts (e.g., full KV cache traces, raw model inputs) are considered production-sensitive and require legal review before sharing.

Open questions & items for engineering/legal:
- Define exact retention windows per deployment type for the canonical audit-log slice used in customer packets (proposal: 90 days default, configurable). Owner: SRE (Liang).
- Add an opt-in field in the RBAC export to include role grant timestamps. Owner: eng-rbac (Marco).
- Standardize redaction rule set (emails, IP hashing, PII heuristics). Owner: security-privacy (Priya).
- Add a curated SIEM mapping template pack for Splunk/Datadog/ELK that can be attached automatically to tickets. Owner: observability team.

Action items (short list):
- Asha: finalize one-page heatmap template and an index of artifacts to attach (due 2025-02-24).
- Marco: prototype RBAC CSV export with grant timestamps (due 2025-03-03).
- Liang: confirm retention policy enforcement and produce a sample audit-log extraction job (due 2025-02-28).
- Priya: draft redaction rules and sample sanitized log generator (due 2025-03-05).

Appendix: Suggested short responses for common questions (copy-paste friendly)
- Q: "Can we get logs sent to our SIEM?"
  A: "Yes. We support both push (Splunk HEC) and pull (S3 delivery) models. We will provide a sample payload and mapping; for Private installs we can integrate directly with your collectors."
- Q: "Do you maintain change history for roles?"
  A: "Yes. RBAC v2 stores role definitions and assignment change events in the audit log. We can export change events for the requested timeframe."
- Q: "How long are logs retained?"
  A: "Default retention is 90 days for hosted. Dedicated and Private offers are configurable per contract; we can export longer ranges on request (subject to storage and SLA)."

Notes to self: keep this doc short; convert heatmap to a one-page PDF that CS can attach. Move final templates into Confluence and link them from the CS playbook.

End of working draft.
